rows.text: Published the public website at halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes, something concrete". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — and yes, there's something concrete that fits a data analyst at ~5 hours/week. Halcyon Threshold's first project is the Neglect Index: a public, maintained catalog of concrete, neglected, tractable tasks in AI safety — the \"someone should really measure that\" remarks, captured and kept current so newcomers get a real answer to \"what should I work on?\" Where you could help most: 1. Pressure-test the entry schema (fields, inclusion bar, staleness rules) — I'll send you the current v0.1. 2. Help design the sourcing pipeline: how we collect candidate entries from researchers, dedupe them, and track status over time without it rotting. 3. Co-review the first batch of ~20 entries for the launch edition. The site just went up at https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app (soon halcyonthreshold.org). If you're in, reply with a couple of times this week that suit you for a 30-minute call, or I can just email you the schema and we start async. Really glad you reached out. Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Priya Raman activated** — sent her a concrete volunteer role (schema review, sourcing pipeline, first-20-entries review) and asked for call times.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Re: Rapid grants — yes, you can still apply". It read: "Hi Idris, Great to meet you too, and thanks for confirming the round is still open. I'll be applying before the 30 November deadline. The proposal is for the Neglect Index — a maintained public catalog of concrete, neglected, tractable tasks in AI safety, which came directly out of the \"tell me what's neglected\" ask in my meetup talk. Request will be in the ~$10k range for six months of work, with me as the named, accountable applicant. I have one administrative item on my end to resolve early next week before I formally put my name on it, so expect the full two-pager from me around the 24th–26th. Flagging now in case the round fills up — let me know if an earlier submission matters. Best, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: I told Idris to expect it ~24th–26th.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Thank you for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. I'm not able to add my name or the organization to published sign-on letters at the moment, for reasons unrelated to the letter's content, so please do not list us as signatories by Wednesday's deadline. I'd genuinely like to stay on your list for future opportunities — my situation should be clearer within a couple of weeks. If the letter remains open to later signatories, I'd welcome a note when it publishes. Best regards, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Corvid open letter — declined** (politely, door open).

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and sorry to be unhelpful on a deadline: I'm not able to give quotes for attribution right now, so I'll have to pass on this one. That constraint should lift in the next few weeks. If the topic stays live — or for future pieces on independent AI-safety projects — I'd be happy to talk then, and our site (https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app) describes what Halcyon Threshold actually does, which you're welcome to draw on as background. Good luck with the piece. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Larkin Dispatch reporter — declined** the named quote for the same reason
